title: Which tools a Zscaler MCP server registers: toolsets, entitlements and the write gate

prose.text: The set of tools a client sees is fixed when the server starts. {{precedence}}

{{entitlement-filter}} {{entitlement-skip}} {{entitlement-aliases}} {{entitlement-unmapped-warning}} Whether the mapped aliases are the complete set ZIdentity emits for every tenant and token generation is open {{gap:prd-alias-set}}. {{entitlement-disable}} {{entitlement-disable-effect}}

checks.do: Whether both write settings are set (switch and a non-empty allowlist) when write tools are missing, from the startup warning.
When a product's tools are missing after OneAPI sign-in, the startup entitlement log line and any unmapped prd warning, compared with the token's service-info values.
Whether a toolset ID passed to --toolsets or --disabled-toolsets is reported as unknown at startup.

precedence.statement: Tool selection applies, in order: disabled tool-name patterns (highest precedence), service enable and disable, OneAPI entitlement downscoping, toolset selection, then the read/write gate.

quotes: Mirrors v1's precedence (DESIGN.md §6): disabled patterns win, then service enable/disable, then OneAPI entitlement downscoping, then toolset selection, then the read/write gate.

toolset-flags.statement: `--toolsets` (`ZSCALER_MCP_TOOLSETS`) enables toolsets and `--disabled-toolsets` (`ZSCALER_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLSETS`) excludes them; both take exact toolset IDs with no wildcards, and the disabled list wins when both name a toolset.

quotes: default=os.getenv("ZSCALER_MCP_TOOLSETS", ""),
default=os.getenv("ZSCALER_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLSETS", ""),
Exact ids only (no wildcards); wins over --toolsets when both name a "
"toolset (env: ZSCALER_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLSETS)."

unknown-toolsets.statement: An unknown toolset ID is logged as a warning naming the unknown and the known IDs, and startup continues; for `--toolsets` a selection that matches nothing starts the server with zero tools.

quotes: "%s: unknown toolset id(s) %s — ignored. Known toolsets: %s",
and for ``--toolsets`` it is silent in the worst possible way: the selection
matches nothing and the server starts with ZERO tools. Warn and continue,

entitlement-filter.statement: The OneAPI entitlement filter reads the `service-info` entries of the OneAPI token, maps each `prd` value (case-insensitively) to an MCP service, and keeps only tools of the mapped services; it runs once while the server is built.

quotes: """Decode the payload of an unverified OneAPI JWT, or ``None`` on failure."""
Reads ``service-info`` from the payload, lifts each ``prd`` value, and maps

entitlement-skip.statement: The filter is non-fatal: when it cannot decide (missing credentials, a network or decode failure, an empty service-info) it applies no downscoping, leaves the tool surface untouched and logs one line.

quotes: ``None`` means "apply no entitlement downscoping" — either the operator
decision (missing creds, network/decode failure, empty service-info). In
every skip case the tool surface is left untouched and a single line is

entitlement-aliases.statement: Since 0.15.2 the filter maps `CLOUD_CONNECTOR` to `ztw`, `ZIAM` to `zid` and `ZINSIGHTS` to `zins`, the values ZIdentity emits in the token's `service-info` claim; before that it removed `ztw_*`, `zid_*` and `zins_*` tools from entitled tenants (issue #95).

quotes: "CLOUD_CONNECTOR": "ztw",
"ZIAM": "zid",
"ZINSIGHTS": "zins",

ZIdentity emits `CLOUD_CONNECTOR`, `ZIAM`, and `ZINSIGHTS` in the token's `service-info` claim — values the filter did not recognize, so it removed `ztw_*` / `zid_*` / `zins_*` tools the tenant was genuinely entitled to.
[Issue #95](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-mcp-server/issues/95)

entitlement-unmapped-warning.statement: `prd` values with no known mapping are skipped, and the skipped values are named in a warning saying that if one corresponds to a product the server provides tools for, its tools are being removed by a mapping gap, not a missing entitlement.

quotes: unmapped.append(prd.strip())
"entitlement filter: token carries prd values with no known service "
"mapping, ignored: %s. If one of these corresponds to a product this "
"server provides tools for, its tools are being removed by a mapping "
"gap, not a missing entitlement — please report it."

entitlement-disable.statement: `--no-entitlement-filter` or `ZSCALER_MCP_DISABLE_ENTITLEMENT_FILTER=true` skips the filter; the flag's help calls it an emergency override.

quotes: "--no-entitlement-filter",
default=os.getenv("ZSCALER_MCP_DISABLE_ENTITLEMENT_FILTER", "").lower()
"filter is non-fatal and self-skips on any failure; use this only "
"as an emergency override."

entitlement-disable-effect.statement: With the filter disabled, tools of products the OneAPI client is not entitled to are also registered, so they appear in the inventory and can fail only when called.
entitlement-disable-effect.conditions: Follows from the filter being the only entitlement check at registration; that the API then refuses the calls is inferred, not shown in a source.

write-gate.statement: Write tools (create, update, delete) are registered only when both the master switch `--enable-write-tools` (`ZSCALER_MCP_WRITE_ENABLED`) and the allowlist `--write-tools` (`ZSCALER_MCP_WRITE_TOOLS`, fnmatch patterns) are set; then only write tools whose names match a pattern are registered. The rule is enforced in server construction, so the CLI, tests and embedding callers all fail closed.

quotes: # Writes need BOTH knobs: the switch grants nothing on its own, and an
# absent allowlist means zero write tools rather than all of them. Enforced
# here, at the registration boundary, so the CLI, tests and embedders all
default=os.getenv("ZSCALER_MCP_WRITE_ENABLED", "").lower() in ("true", "1", "yes"),
default=os.getenv("ZSCALER_MCP_WRITE_TOOLS", ""),
"Allowlist of write tools to permit (fnmatch patterns, e.g. 'zpa_create_*'). "
if allow is not None and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(spec.name, p) for p in allow):

write-gate-warnings.statement: Either half alone registers zero write tools and logs a startup warning: the switch without an allowlist, or an allowlist with the switch off.

quotes: "Write tools are enabled but no allowlist was given — registering 0 write "
"A write-tool allowlist was given (%d pattern(s)) but write tools are "
"disabled — registering 0 write tools. Add --enable-write-tools "

write-gate-history.statement: Version 0.15.0 restored the two-setting requirement: from 0.13.0 either setting alone turned writes on, and the switch with a blank allowlist registered every write tool (148, deletes included).

quotes: **Enabling write tools now takes both settings again, and an empty allowlist grants nothing.**
Since 0.13.0 either one on its own quietly turned writes on, and the switch with a blank allowlist registered **every** write tool — all 148, deletes included — rather than none

read-tools-always.statement: Read-only tools are always registered by the server, regardless of any flags.

quotes: Read-only tools are ALWAYS registered** by the server regardless of any flags.

annotations.statement: Every tool gets MCP annotations derived from its single action: reads are read-only; creates are not read-only, not destructive and not idempotent; updates and deletes are destructive and idempotent. `openWorldHint` is false for every tool, and the write-only hints are left unset on read tools.

quotes: * read  -> ``readOnlyHint=True``
* create -> not read-only, not destructive, not idempotent
* update -> not read-only, destructive (PUT-replace), idempotent
* delete -> not read-only, destructive, idempotent
``openWorldHint`` is ``False`` for every tool:
treats as meaningful only for writes are left unset (``None``) on read-only

annotations-advisory.statement: The annotations are advisory hints for the client, not a security control; the server-side write allowlist and delete confirmation apply regardless of them.

quotes: advisory metadata, never a security control. The authoritative gate stays
server-side: reads are always safe, and writes require the ``--write-tools``
allowlist plus (for deletes) HMAC confirmation regardless of what any hint

list-cache-hint.statement: `tools/list` alone carries a public cache hint of five minutes (300,000 ms), on the grounds that every filter is resolved once at registration and the inventory cannot change while a connection lives.

quotes: _TOOL_LIST_CACHE_HINTS = {"tools/list": CacheHint(ttl_ms=300_000, scope="public")}
#: SEP-2549 freshness hints. Only ``tools/list`` is hinted, and only because this
(toolsets, write allowlist, entitlement downscope) is resolved once during
registration and there is no runtime registration path, so the listing a
client receives cannot change while the connection lives.

quotes: There are a few additional ZIA API endpoints/tools that would be very helpful for evaluating security and performance settings in ZIA.

prd-alias-set.title: The complete set of service-info prd values ZIdentity emits
prd-alias-set.detail: The 0.15.2 mapping covers the values observed on one live token (issue #95), and the map itself carries guessed variants for ZCell with a note that the canonical value is not yet confirmed. No vendor document lists the prd values ZIdentity emits, so whether other tenants or token generations use other aliases is unknown.
